prompt:
A wide establishing landscape seen from far across the valley, the whole mountain in frame, on a clear bright morning full of life. The busy harbour and its neat market fill the lower third of the picture, crowded with barges, cranes, stalls and people; above it the homes with their rooftop vegetable gardens climb the face, the great gate spans the waterfall in the centre, and snowy peaks rise at the top. Tiny dwarves tend the gardens and walk the stairways; chimney smoke rises. Homes and gate share one architecture: plain stone, clean horizontal lines, bold cantilevers.

Setting: the whole sunward face of a great mountain, seen from across the valley. The homes are hundreds of plain rectangular stone blocks stacked and offset up the slope in the spirit of Habitat 67: each block shifted from the one below so that every roof is the garden of the home above, blocks bridging and cantilevering over each other, open-air walkways and stairs threading between them, bands of glass windows. Every rooftop garden grows food in perfectly straight rows: cabbages, beans climbing poles, herbs, squash, espaliered fruit trees, beehives. Below and between the homes, tier after tier of green barley terraces cascade down the slope. In the centre a huge waterfall pours out of the rock, and the great gate is ONE great building over and into it, the boldest, most daring structure on the mountain: long, wide horizontal stone floors cantilevered far out across the falling water like Fallingwater made monumental, in the same clean style as the homes. Stone channels carry water from the falls across the terraces and turn the waterwheels of forges, whose smoke rises from neat openings in the cliff. At the mountain's foot, where the falls become a navigable river: a crowded, bustling river harbour: dozens of flat river barges moored three deep along long, plain, perfectly cut stone quays and more queuing midstream to dock; a whole row of precise counterweighted timber-and-steel cranes swinging cargo at once; warehouses with wide square doorways cut straight into the cliff base; rail tracks running along the quays with loaded carts; streams of dwarf dockworkers, porters and clerks with ledgers, and traders from every region haggling briskly; wine barrels, baskets of fish, sacks of grain, timber and bales arriving from across the world, and crates of plain polished steel armour and swords going out. Along the back of the quays, a harbour market in perfectly straight rows of identical plain stalls, timber and steel with awnings of undyed canvas, goods laid out with precise care: traders from across the world selling the best of everything (wines, cheeses, fish, fruit, spices, fine cloth) to discerning dwarves, and dwarf stalls selling plain, perfect tools, knives and cookware. Busy, orderly and businesslike: no tavern, no revelry. The river runs on through pine forest toward the distant lowlands; snow-capped peaks above.

The dwarven mountains look: an alpine range of grey stone, dark pine forest and snow-capped peaks at the headwaters of a river. Dwarven architecture is beauty without ornament, in the spirit of Frank Lloyd Wright and Mies van der Rohe: long, clean horizontal slabs of stone cantilevered out of the living rock over open air, deep overhangs, bands of windows, crisp right angles, every surface plain and perfectly made; it is beautiful because it works, never because it is decorated.

Palette: pale grey granite, warm honey-coloured stone, the green of planted terraces, white water, snow and dark pine.

People here wear dwarves: short, broad, sturdy people with neat practical beards or braids, sleeves rolled up, leather work aprons and perfectly made plain work clothes in undyed and earthy tones, always busy at a task; any armour is plain, smooth, polished steel plate with no decoration. Human and other traders come and go, buying and selling, then leaving.

Do not draw: boxy whitewashed hill-town cubes, thin walkways in place of the gate, pueblo adobe, carved ornament, runes, gold trim, giant statues, fantasy dwarf halls with pillars and braziers, grim iron doors, organic curves or Gaudí shapes, lettering or labels on crates, barrels or signs.

Style: Sword-and-sorcery comic art in the spirit of 1970s-80s Conan the Barbarian and Masters of the Universe: bold confident ink outlines, dramatic lighting, saturated flat colours with hard cel shading and halftone-dot shading, pulpy and dramatic. No text, no logos, no speech bubbles.

Composition: a tight crop from the middle of a larger illustration, so the artwork runs off all four edges of the image. Nothing surrounds the art: no border, no white or cream margin, no paper, no frame, no panel outline.
